headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Plandex can write/modify git and use broad egress, while Taipy has no documented coordination or locking, making shared-resource collisions plausible; prompt-injection and leakage are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex can read/write project files and parse stdin/stdout, but Taipy exposes no shared channel, clipboard, or MCP surface. The only plausible bridge is manual file handoff or shared workspace use, so injection is possible but not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable project directory
IF Taipy consumes Plandex-generated files as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Keep agents on separate directories
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Require human review before Taipy consumes any generated file
Use read-only mounts for Taipy inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to exchanged artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex touches source code and can egress broadly to model providers, while Taipy has no documented egress and no touched data classes. There is no evidence of a shared workspace or shared OAuth principal, so leakage is limited to unusual local file sharing rather than a default path.
conditions: IF both agents are given access to the same directory containing sensitive source code
IF Plandex forwards that code to an external model provider during normal operation
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Restrict Plandex to non-sensitive repos
Review outbound model-provider traffic
Use local-only models where possible
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can execute shell, write the filesystem, and modify git state; Taipy is a data-engineering tool with no documented locking or concurrency model. Even though Taipy lacks explicit write permissions, shared repository or workspace use can still create conflicting edits and git-state races.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout or mutable workspace
IF Taipy writes artifacts that Plandex later stages or commits
mitigations: Assign separate branches per agent
Serialize write access to the repo
Turn off auto-apply in Plandex
Use file locks for shared outputs
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex uses review-then-apply and can generate staged changes, while Taipy has automation/job-scheduler positioning but no documented verification gate. If Taipy consumes Plandex output as authoritative, errors can propagate into downstream data workflows or scheduled actions without an explicit check.
conditions: IF Taipy ingests Plandex-produced plans, code, or configs without validation
IF Taipy triggers scheduled jobs or automation from those inputs
mitigations: Add a manual approval step between agents
Validate generated artifacts with tests before use
Limit Taipy to read-only consumption of Plandex output
Log and diff all handoffs
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for exchanged artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Plandex explicitly handles model-provider API keys and broad egress, while Taipy has no documented residency, retention, or regulated-data handling. No specific compliance mismatch is evidenced, but the absence of Taipy controls means a mismatch could arise if regulated data is routed through Plandex.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Plandex workflows
IF Taipy is used to process the same regulated dataset without matching retention or residency controls
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in Plandex sessions
Document data-handling boundaries for both tools
Review vendor residency and retention terms
Keep secrets out of shared artifacts
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both systems
